head.t: Prevalence of degenerative mitral valve disease growing rapidly globally
head.x: The global prevalence of patients with degenerative mitral valve disease more than doubled to 16.1 million cases with an attributed 39,800 deaths in 2023. Moreover, mortality and disability were worse in women and low-resource areas, highlighting the need for affordable diagnostic and treatment tools.

head.t: Ultrasound-guided vascular access training using gelatin-based simulation models – Full Text
head.x: "Gelatin-based models are low-cost, accessible, and well accepted as tools for ultrasound-guided vascular access training. They may help skill acquisition and confidence, even among clinicians with previous experience, and are particularly suited for use in resource-limited settings" Ferreira et al (2026).

head.t: Improving CLABSI prevention requires multilevel strategies
head.x: "Improving CLABSI prevention may require multilevel strategies that combine targeted education and training, adequate resource allocation, leadership engagement, standardized clinical procedures, and ongoing audit and feedback" Shi et al (2026).

head.t: New evidence hub offers a single source for data and research
head.x: We are pleased to introduce our new RNID evidence hub, bringing together research, data, and insights from people with lived experience in a single resource. It's the first evidence hub dedicated to providing in-depth evidence and research about people who are deaf, have hearing loss or tinnitus.

f.t: PRISM: incorporating advanced imaging technologies into a comprehensive strategy for hard-to-heal wound assessment and management
f.x: Head-to-heal wounds—particularly diabetic lower-extremity wounds—remain among the most challenging and resource-intensive problems in contemporary healthcare, with five-year recurrence rates of 40–65% and a trajectory toward amputation that is frequently driven by three interacting and often under-recognised failures…

f.t: An online learning resource in support of the recruitment of people living with dementia and their carers to research
f.x: Although the number of people diagnosed with dementia is increasing globally, it is estimated that only 2% are engaged in dementia research in the UK. In part, this may be due to a lack of confidence on the part of health and social care professionals to discuss research opportunities.
